Location Algorfa, located in the Vega Baja del Segura region, has a rich history dating back to Roman times. The name of the city comes from the Arabic word 'Al-Gorfa', meaning 'cave', as the area was known for its numerous natural caves. Today, Algorfa is known for its production of citrus fruits and vegetables. Algorfa is home to many attractions that will appeal to visitors of all ages. Here are just a few of the most important ones and: La Finca Golf Course If you're a golf fan, La Finca Golf Course is a must-visit place. Plaza de Espana Plaza de España is Algorfa's main square and is a great place to soak up the local atmosphere. Here you will find a beautiful fountain, plenty of seating and plenty of restaurants and bars. It's the perfect place to relax with a drink and enjoy the local culture.

property.description: Penthouse for sale in Villajoyosa. Discover with us a modern estate hidden in a beautiful corner of the picturesque Costa Blanca, right next to a natural beach surrounded by majestic mountains. Your new Spanish apartment is located just 2 km from the center of Villajoyosa and 10 km from the popular Benidorm. Fall in love and live in this idyllic place, surrounded by nature. Imagine that right in front of your house there is a beautiful beach with crystal clear and calm water, the main character of which is turquoise blue. Choose from modern 2 and 3 bedroom apartments with large terraces and complete urbanization including a social club, gym and swimming pool. Near your new home, just a few minutes away you will find shopping centers, a hospital and all kinds of services. Contact us and take advantage of a unique opportunity to live or relax in a magical place! It is also an excellent investment opportunity! Location Villajoyosa is a hidden pearl on Spain's Costa Blanca. This colorful fishing village is located between the popular town of Benidorm and El Campello, approximately 30 minutes' drive from Alicante Airport. Villajoyosa seems to literally hang on the rocky seaside cliffs. Combined with the charming architecture, it gives an amazing impression of a picturesque coast. What's more, the name of the town itself promises a nice time. Villajoyosa or La Vila Joiosa literally means a joyful town. This is indeed the impression it gives, with its colorful houses in the city center. Urban legend has it that the buildings were painted in bold colors to help fishermen find their way home. Today they certainly attract crowds of tourists and are an inspiration for many photographers and artists. In recent years, this charming town has become a desirable place for people looking for a second home in a quiet area. Villajoyosa has a lot to offer, from the wide sandy beach to the narrow and colorful streets of the historic center. Villajoyosa has been associated with chocolate since the 19th century. This is where the popular Spanish chocolate factory Valor is located. The Valor, Pérez and Clavileño museums are must-sees. There you will learn everything about the chocolate production process and its history in this area. Trips led by knowledgeable guides are most often combined with chocolate tasting. During the holiday season, Villajoyosa hosts various cultural events. It is worth visiting the village in July, when the famous Moors and Christians festival takes place here. The main attraction is the reconstruction of the battle from 1538, as well as concerts, performances and shows. Villajoyosa contains 3 km of beaches with golden sand and views of the endless clear sea. The most beautiful of them are playa El Paraíso, Xarco and la Caleta. Here you will find both larger tourist resorts and hidden, mysterious corners perfect for peaceful relaxation. The seaside panorama, Mediterranean climate and soft, hot sand perfectly create an atmosphere of complete relaxation. Near the beaches you will find regional restaurants and cafes offering fresh Mediterranean delicacies. Villajoyosa delights tourists with its idyllic, cheerful atmosphere and colorful houses. There is no shortage of attractions for people looking for experiences and interesting history and culture. Just walking along the seaside provides stunning views and impressions that are hard to forget.

San Pedro de Alcántara and Marbella are 16 kilometres apart and the famous Puerto Banús is less than 9 kilometres from this picturesque town. Restaurants San Pedro also welcomes an increasing number of tourists who come to eat and socialise, thanks to the large variety of tapas bars, cafés and traditional restaurants in the old town and the growing selection of excellent tapas restaurants and eateries around the boulevard and Paseo Marítimo , offering everything from Spanish cuisine to Italian, French, Argentinian and Asian cuisine. The football club attracts many young players and there are many excellent golf courses within a ten-minute drive, including Los Arqueros, El Higueral, La Zagaleta, La Quinta, Magna Marbella, Los Naranjos, Las Brisas, Aloha Golf, Dama de Noche, Guadalmina, Atalaya and El Campanario. Among the palm trees, we can highlight an interesting sculpture, a life-size elephant, joyfully striding along the beach. As expected, this elephant has become one of the most popular features of the beach and one of the most photographed by visitors. San Pedro de Alcántara beach is 1,400 metres long and has an average width of around 35 metres. A remarkable beach whose qualities have earned it the Blue Flag award for 24 years. Just as it has once again received the Q for tourist quality, clear symbols of the good condition of this beach.

The flats in this new development have been designed using modern materials, bright spaces and an optimal layout, ideal both as a main residence and as a second home or holiday rental investment. Planned completion date: mid or end of 2027 Location Pulpí, the first coastal town in Andalusia, located on the border between Murcia and Almería, is one of the most picturesque and idyllic landscapes in Spain and offers many different reasons to visit. The municipality, located in the north-eastern part of the province, has three clearly differentiated areas within its territory: the coastal area, the inland basin and the small chain of mountain ranges separating them. Pulpí Geode In addition to its spectacular beaches and coves, there is a real natural gem here, which since its opening to the public in 2019 has become a tourist attraction: the Geode. Located in Mina Rica, in Pilar de Jaravía, it is a giant geode approximately eight metres long and two metres high. It is the second largest in the world after the Chihuahua Crystal Cave in Mexico and the largest of the geodes that can be visited. Other places to visit There is much more to visit in Pulpí. The town of Pulpí is home to the Church of San Miguel, the second oldest building in the municipality, dating from 1801, and also the tallest, with a spectacular altar. Also noteworthy are the Benzal Picnic and Ethnographic Area and the Apartadero Viewpoint. Also worth visiting are the Scenic Space with the Pintor Pedro Antonio Martínez Room, which houses a collection of paintings by the influential Pulpileño painter, and the Black Room, the largest of its kind in Europe, which houses a spectacular collection of 1,000 luminescent minerals. Beaches Almería also boasts a catalogue of spectacular beaches and coves. The 13 beaches in Pulpí run along the coastline from north to south: Los Cocedores Beach, Las Palmeras Beach, La Carolina Beach, Invencible Cove, Costa Tranquila Cove, Cuartel Cove, Tía Antonia Cove, Rincón de los Nudos Cove, Mar Rabiosa Beach, Mar Serena Beach, Calypso Beach, La Entrevista Beach and Los Nardos Beach. Four of the five beaches located further south are Blue Flag beaches due to the quality of their services and their crystal-clear waters, which are excellent at all of them. These are Mar Serena, Mar Rabiosa, Calypso and Los Nardos.
